Text.Text: Killzone Beacon, designation closed, file complete. You're released from this briefing and from my ledger. Carry the doctrine correctly; the Republic does not reissue this clearance twice.
This needs rank 50 in Devices. Finish your training, then report back. I won't put you in charge of fire you can't control.

An unauthorized cell is conducting live fire tests in the Republic Engineering Bunker. Six Killzone Beacon adepts hold the perimeter. Defeat them and recover their docket. I need the firing orders before I can shut the tests down.
Take the bunker key to the entrance on the Republic Base combat deck. Check your escape route before you start clearing the perimeter.

It marks a kill zone before the enemy occupies it, so fire converges the instant they do. Effective doctrine in the right hands. In the wrong hands it paints friendly positions just as easily, which is why it cannot leak.
That docket is the Republic's own filing on bunker fire-control assets. If it's in that cell's hands, someone with clearance handed it to them, and I need a name before I need a court-martial.
Six adepts, standard live-fire discipline, nothing you haven't handled. Treat every marker in that bunker as active. This is not a drill and I will not pretend it is one to make you comfortable.
Six adepts in the Republic Engineering Bunker. Recover the docket and report to me at the base entrance.
Confirm the docket is intact and hand it over for verification.
Verified. Six hostiles down, docket intact, and a name I'll be following up on privately. Payment's logged. Good first briefing.

Five specialists are controlling the bunker shield grid. They've been using it to shape the killing ground. Defeat the five and recover their relay. We'll see whether the test reports account for everyone caught inside.
Recover the relay. Watch the firing lanes before crossing them.
It keeps broadcasting kill-zone geometry to whoever's listening. Eventually that's every hostile force on Viscara with a receiver. I want it silent before that happens.
Shield grids and targeting grids share the same backbone in bunker installations. Whoever repurposed it knew that. That's not a lucky guess, that's someone with Republic training.
Five, dug in around the relay itself. They'll defend it like it's worth more than their own lives. To them, right now, it is.
Five specialists hold the shield relay inside the bunker. Recover it after they're defeated.
Confirm relay status and hand it over.
Confirmed silent. That's two objectives clean. You're proving reliable enough that I'm considering trusting you with the part of this briefing I haven't said out loud yet.

The warden controls access to the bunker. Challenge him there and recover his command crest when he's defeated. Bring support if you have it. His fire control is good; don't let him choose where all of you stand.
Granted. Take the time you need. I would rather delay this briefing than close it with your name on a casualty report.
People who can cover you when you're occupied with the beacon. Choose support that can work together. More bodies in a firing lane don't make a better team.
Cracked like that, under load, which means he's been running live command scenarios longer than any bunker range should allow. I want to know exactly how long.

Textbook, which is what makes him dangerous. He's not improvising. He's running Republic tactics against Republic-trained targets, which means he's had exactly the kind of teacher I'm afraid he's had.
Use the bunker challenge marker to call the warden. Defeat him and bring back his command crest.
Confirm the warden is neutralized and the crest is secured.
The crest confirms his authority. Good work. Take your pay and check your gear. The officers still supplying these tests are next.

Four officers still have the quartermaster's override chip. They can keep these tests supplied indefinitely. Defeat the four inside the bunker and recover it. I'm cutting their ammunition off at the source.
Bring the override chip here. I'm cutting the tests off before another requisition clears.
Every requisition override, timestamped, cross-referenced against a quartermaster's signature. It's the paper trail that turns a rogue cell into a court-martial.
Someone with enough rank to move bunker hardware without a second signature. That's a short list. I've narrowed it further than I'm comfortable admitting.
Recommended. Four hostiles is worse odds than one warden in some respects. Keep your fire team intact; I don't reissue clearances for replacements mid-briefing.
Four officers in the bunker still control the override chip. Recover it and return here.
Confirm the chip and hand it over for cross-reference.
Cross-referenced. The signature is one I recognize, and I don't like what that means for the fifth objective. Command's been compromised further up than I want to say out loud yet.

The master is in the Engineering Command Room. Use the challenge marker to call him and defeat him. He's used to seeing people move where his fire sends them. Keep your own route, then report back to the base entrance.
Take it. I would rather you go in ready than go in on my schedule. This briefing ends when the objective is actually secure, not before.
Command's own staging ground, if his projections hold. He's not testing anymore. He's rehearsing a strike against people who trust that ground is safe.
From this briefing room, originally, back when I still thought doctrine couldn't be misused by someone who understood it well enough. I was wrong. I've stopped pretending otherwise.

Then the doctrine gets reissued, correctly, to someone who reads a grid reference and sees people worth protecting, not targets worth painting. That would be you, assuming this goes the way I need it to.
Call the master in the Engineering Command Room. Defeat him, then report back to the Republic Base entrance.
Confirm status. Is the objective secure?
Live tests suspended. Supplies secured. Good work. Your pay is authorized, and I'll take you through Killzone Beacon when you're ready. We'll begin with choosing where your people can get out.
Back to the briefing.
Understood. Moving on the objective.
What does a killzone beacon actually do?
Why does this docket matter to the Republic?
What's the risk profile on site?
Not cleared for this yet. Standing by.
Docket recovered, here it is.
Back to the briefing.
Copy. Moving to intercept the relay.
What happens if that relay stays active?
Why is a shield grid relay tied to targeting?
How many specialists am I looking at?
Requesting delay before deployment.
Relay's down, here it is.
Back to the briefing.
I'll assemble support and challenge him.
What support would you recommend?
What does the crest tell you?
What's the warden's command style?
Requesting time to assemble a team.
Crest secured, warden down.
Back to the briefing.
Copy. Moving on the inner circle.
What's on a quartermaster override chip?
Who signs off on requisitions like this?
Should I deploy with the same team?
Requesting a briefing delay.
Chip secured, here it is.
Back to the briefing.
Team of three, and we finish this properly.
What position is he planning to paint?
Where did he learn this doctrine?
What happens to the doctrine after this?
Requesting more time before final deployment.
Objective secure. He's down.
